Allow Vikify to route your traffic?

Vikify uses Android VPN to route other apps’ IPv4 traffic, including DNS requests, through an encrypted tunnel to the server in your selected profile. This gives your VPN provider access to your IP address, destination addresses, connection times and traffic volume to deliver the connection. The provider can read traffic that has no end-to-end encryption. Vikify does not sell traffic or use it for advertising. You can disconnect at any time and withdraw this consent in Help.

Add an HTTPS subscription from your provider, a VLESS link or a Base64 list. You can paste text, scan a QR code or choose an image. Supported transports: REALITY, XHTTP/TLS and WebSocket/TLS.

For mixed lists, review the skipped entries before importing compatible profiles. One subscription or saved set of profiles is active at a time.

Choose a profile, tap Connect and accept the VPN disclosure and Android request. If a profile fails, try another compatible profile.

HTTPS subscriptions update daily when Android permits background work, or when you tap Update. Profiles imported directly from text have no remote update address: replace them with new links.

The server routes new connections through the primary node, or the backup when it is unavailable. Reconnect if an existing connection drops.
Connects directly to the primary server using REALITY. Start with this profile; try the backup options if it is unavailable.
Connects directly to a separate backup server using REALITY. Try this if the primary server is unavailable.
Uses another REALITY port on the primary server. This may help if your network restricts the main port; it still uses the same server.
Uses XHTTP with TLS encryption. Try this transport if REALITY profiles do not work on your network.
Uses WebSocket with TLS encryption. An additional fallback if REALITY and XHTTP are unavailable.
Uses VLESS with REALITY protection. Availability depends on the server and restrictions on your current network.
